entities.name: Acacius
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Acacius (died 496) was Catholicos of Seleucia-Ctesiphon and Patriarch of the Church of the East from 485 to 496, one of the most significant leaders in the history of Mesopotamian Christianity. His patriarchate was marked by two decisive acts that shaped the Eastern Church for centuries: the Synod of Beth Lapat (484–486) and his formalisation of the Church of the East's Nestorian theological identity.

At the Synod of Beth Lapat, Acacius presided over the formal adoption of Nestorianism — the Christological position condemned at the Council of Ephesus (431) — as the official theology of the Church of the East. This decision permanently separated the Persian Church from the Greek Chalcedonian orthodoxy and aligned the Church of the East with the theology of Theodore of Mopsuestia and Nestorius. The separation had both theological and political dimensions: as subjects of the Sassanid Persian Empire, Christians who rejected Roman Catholic orthodoxy were more useful to the Persian state.

Acacius also addressed the Church's internal structure, including the question of clerical marriage and property. His patriarchate established the theological and institutional framework within which the Church of the East would expand dramatically across Central Asia, India, and China over the following centuries, becoming one of the most geographically extensive Christian bodies in world history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Patriarch of the Church of the East who formalised its Nestorian identity at the Synod of Beth Lapat, permanently separating it from Chalcedonian orthodoxy and establishing the theological framework for its remarkable expansion across Asia.
